newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Costello sees low interest rate growth.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Costello sees low interest rate growth.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that fresh economic data showed the country was set for stronger, low interest rate, low inflation economic growth.

Costello said private demand indicators were strong and the only detraction to growth was stocks (inventories), which would be corrected in the June quarter to deliver growth one percent or above. "...Strengthening growth, low-inflation growth, low-interest rate growth," he told parliament.
"They are the kinds of conditions that you would actually want to see in the Australian economy," Costello said.

Official data released earlier on Wednesday showed Australia's seasonally adjusted average gross domestic product, which averages income, expenditure and production measures of GDP, rose 0.9 percent in the March quarter.
Real GDP-A in the year to March rose 2.4 percent. Most economists had forecast March quarter GDP-A to rise around 0.8 percent, for a year-on-year increase of about 2.2 percent.
In its May 13 budget, the government forecast GDP growth of 3.25 percent, year average, for the fiscal year to June 30, 1997, and 3.75 percent in 1997/98.
It also projected consumer price index inflation of 1.0 percent, year average, in 1997/98.
The Reserve Bank has cut official cash rates a total two percentage points in four separate cuts since July 1996.
